argument_quality.justification: The Pro side presents a coherent economic case centered on tax bases and the 'multiplier effect' of high-tech growth.

evidence_grounding.justification: The arguments rely on plausible economic concepts, though they remain somewhat abstract compared to the specific resource-drain concerns of the opposition.

steelman_fidelity.justification: The Pro side explicitly acknowledges and attempts to address the 'socialized' costs and 'transient' nature of the jobs.

rebuttal_effectiveness.justification: The Pro side successfully pivoted the infrastructure cost argument into a narrative of modernization, though they struggled to fully address the 'ghost facility' point.

clarity.justification: The case is easy to follow with clear, logical transitions between paragraphs.

argument_quality.justification: The Con side offers a very strong critique of the externalities (water/power) and the fiscal risks of relying on multinational corporations.

evidence_grounding.justification: The inclusion of 'ghost' facilities as a specific critique makes the case more grounded in real-world industry concerns.

steelman_fidelity.justification: The Con side accurately identifies the core of the Pro's arguments (multipliers and opportunity costs) before systematically dismantling them.

rebuttal_effectiveness.justification: The Con side was highly effective at deconstructing the Pro's 'multiplier' and 'opportunity cost' claims by identifying them as fiscal gambles or false dilemmas.

clarity.justification: The argument is extremely clear and follows a logical progression from resource reality to fiscal prudence.
